sections.html:
A Colony homeowner can hire an agent, take a cash offer, or arrange an as-is sale. Values here run well above those in many Texas cities, so the gap between a fast sale and a full-price listing can be wide. Work out what you would net on each path before choosing.

The Colony is a young city, with its first homes dating from the mid-1970s. Resale houses compete with newer construction, and a seller with a dated interior often faces buyers who measure the place against fresh builds nearby. Selling as is for cash can spare you the cost of updating.

  • Agent route: strongest for a move-in-ready house in a good school zone.
  • Cash route: strongest when time, repairs or a move date are your main worries.
  • Rent out or hold: only sensible if the carrying costs work for you.

The city began as a planned community on the eastern shore of Lake Lewisville. The first families moved in during October 1974, and the city incorporated in 1977 before becoming a home rule city in 1979. Eastvale, a lakeside community begun in the early 1960s, folded into the city in 1987.

The useful part for a seller is age. Houses from the first building wave are now decades old, so roofs, windows and plumbing are what buyers check first. Newer sections nearer the Grandscape and State Highway 121 area draw a different crowd than the older lakeside streets.

The Colony had 46,196 residents in July 2025, up 3.7 percent from 2020. Density was 3,179 residents per square mile in 2020 on 14.01 square miles.

With household income above $114,000 and a long average commute, buyers tend to be dual-income households working across the Dallas-Fort Worth area. Price your house against recent nearby sales rather than county-wide averages.

Nebraska Furniture Mart of Texas opened in spring 2015 and anchors the 433-acre Grandscape project in the State Highway 121 corridor. Topgolf, Scheels and Galaxy Theatres are part of the mix, and the city estimates six to eight million visitors a year. Trails and green space, Tree City USA and Playful City USA designations, and a spot 35 minutes from downtown Dallas and 25 minutes from DFW International Airport complete the pitch.

  • Buyers near Grandscape and SH 121 weigh traffic and walkability.
  • Buyers near the lakeshore weigh trails and park access.
  • Commuters compare the 27.1-minute average drive with other suburbs.

sections.h2: Who taxes and bills a Colony address
sections.html:
Three offices are involved. The city council sets its rate during the budget process each September. Denton Central Appraisal District sets the value and grants exemptions. The Denton County Tax Assessor/Collector bills and collects. Tax is levied on October 1 against the value as of the prior January 1. Ask the city finance office or the county tax office for the current rate.

  • Denton CAD: 3911 Morse St. in Denton, 940-349-3800, mailing address P.O. Box 2816, Denton, TX 76202.
  • County tax office: 940-349-3500 in Denton and 940-349-3510 at the Frisco Government Center, 5535 F.M. 423.
  • City finance office: 6053 Main Street, 972-624-3140.

Taxes unpaid after January 31 turn delinquent on February 1 with a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest. The lien attaches on January 1 and follows the property to a buyer, so the title company pays any balance out of your proceeds.

The city's homestead exemption is 5 percent of the property's market value, and the dollar amount moves when market value moves. If you receive a notice that an exemption was reduced or cancelled from the prior year, check the exemption code in the table it contains and review your status at the Denton CAD website. The notice alone does not mean a taxing unit changed its policy.

  • A statewide school exemption of $140,000 applies, with extra relief for seniors and disabled owners.
  • Applications are due by April 30 in most cases.
  • A buyer who moves in after January 1 can claim the exemption for the rest of that year when the prior owner had none.

The city exemption covers owner-occupied homes only, not rentals or investment property.

Gather the lender payoff, the tax bill and any owners' association papers first. Then pick a route, sign a contract and open title.

  • Request a lender payoff and check for liens of record.
  • Settle taxes through the closing date.
  • Sign the deed in front of a notary so the clerk can accept it.
  • File it in Denton County, where most of The Colony lies.

Recording charges follow a statutory fee schedule, and your closing statement shows the actual amount. If an HOA governs your street, ask early for its payoff or transfer letter, since a missing HOA statement is a common reason closings slip by a few days.

An heir has four years from the death to probate a will. Some estates use a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit or a recorded transfer on death deed. A Texas probate attorney can tell you which fits.

Foreclosure auctions follow a first-Tuesday schedule with 21 days' notice, so selling beforehand can keep your equity. A landlord must give written notice to vacate, at least three days unless the lease says otherwise, then file in justice court, where trial is set between 10 and 21 days after filing. A writ of possession can follow six days after final judgment. Plan the sale around those timelines.

faqs.q: Which county is The Colony in for tax and deed purposes?
faqs.a: Denton County, for most of the city. Denton Central Appraisal District values property and the Denton County tax office collects, with a satellite office in Frisco. Confirm the county on your own tax bill.

faqs.q: Does The Colony have its own homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's homestead exemption is 5 percent of market value, and school districts add the statewide $140,000 exemption. Apply through Denton CAD by April 30.

faqs.q: Should I update my house before selling in The Colony?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Cash buyers purchase as is. If you list, weigh the cost of updates against the price difference, since buyers often compare your house with newer homes nearby.

faqs.q: How do I find The Colony's current tax rate?
faqs.a: Ask the city finance office at 972-624-3140 or the Denton County tax office at 940-349-3500. The city sets its rate each September.

faqs.q: Can I sell if I have not paid last year's property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance, with penalty and interest, is taken out of the proceeds when you close. Request a payoff figure good through your closing date.
